meta.title: Geography, Access, Transit & Development Pipeline
meta.note: A QSR freehold is worth its drive-thru. Access, visibility, congestion and the pipeline of competing or complementary development therefore dominate value. Everything parcel-specific is left blank and flagged because the address is withheld.

rows.m: Official planning geography covering central Los Angeles
rows.v: Downtown Community Plan Area = Central City Community Plan Area + Central City North Community Plan Area
rows.p: Downtown Community Plan update (CEQA ENV-2017-433-EIR, SCH No. 2017021024)
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning
rows.n: Case Nos. CPC-2017-432-CPU and CPC-2014-1582-CA; Council Districts 1, 9 and 14.

rows.m: Central City Community Plan Area — boundaries
rows.v: North: Sunset Boulevard / Cesar Chavez Avenue. South: Santa Monica Freeway (I-10). West: Harbor Freeway (I-110). East: Alameda Street.
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning
rows.n: Approximately 2,161 acres. Includes Civic Center, Fashion District, Financial District, Historic Core, Little Tokyo and Skid Row. The plan in effect was adopted in 2003 and an update is underway.

rows.m: Central City North Community Plan Area — boundaries
rows.v: North: Stadium Way, Lilac Terrace and North Broadway. South: City of Vernon. West: Alameda Street. East: Los Angeles River.
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning
rows.n: Approximately 2,005 acres.

rows.m: Downtown Community Plan — horizon and intent
rows.v: Intended to guide development through the year 2040
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning
rows.n: The plan horizon extends beyond the 2030-2035 lease expiry — a re-tenanting or redevelopment decision taken at expiry will be assessed against this adopted plan.

rows.m: Communities bordering the Downtown Plan Area
rows.v: Boyle Heights, Silver Lake-Echo Park, Westlake, Southeast Los Angeles, South Los Angeles, and the City of Vernon
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning

rows.m: Metro D Line (Purple) Subway Extension — Section 1 revenue service
rows.s: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) — D Line Subway Extension project page
rows.n: Three new underground stations: Wilshire/La Brea, Wilshire/Fairfax and Wilshire/La Cienega. Extends subway service west along Wilshire Boulevard from Koreatown.

rows.m: Metro D Line Extension — Sections 2 and 3
rows.v: Under construction; Section 2 serves Beverly Hills and Century City, Section 3 reaches Westwood and the VA campus
rows.s: Los Angeles Metro — D Line Subway Extension project page
rows.n: Metro states 'Work continues across all three sections of the project.'

rows.m: Metro D Line Extension — revenue opening year for Sections 2 and 3
rows.s: Los Angeles Metro
rows.n: LEFT BLANK. The 2027 date was found only on non-official pages; the official Metro project page retrieved in this session does not state a year for Sections 2 and 3. Not published as fact. FLAG F-15.

rows.m: Statewide housing unit growth
rows.v: +0.77% in 2025 (down from +0.84% in 2024); 115,165 net units added; total 15,064,131
rows.s: California Department of Finance, 2026 Estimates E-1 press release
rows.n: First time California has recorded over 15 million housing units. Includes 29,710 ADUs (+11.42% year over year).

rows.m: Los Angeles County — net housing units added
rows.v: +11,260 (ranked 1st among California counties by net housing gain)
rows.s: California Department of Finance, 2026 Estimates E-1 press release
rows.n: City of Los Angeles added 7,061 multi-family units = 62.7% of its net housing growth. New multifamily near a subject site is additive to trade-area demand.

rows.m: Housing units lost to fire statewide
rows.v: 11,406 (including 11,160 lost to the Eaton and Palisades fires)
rows.s: California Department of Finance, 2026 Estimates E-1 press release
rows.n: Quantifies the housing-stock destruction side of the January 2025 wildfire event.

rows.m: Los Angeles County — number of cities with population change in 2025
rows.v: 148 cities gained population, 333 lost population, 2 unchanged (Monte Sereno in Santa Clara County and Industry in Los Angeles County)
rows.s: California Department of Finance, 2026 Estimates E-1 press release
rows.n: Statewide. Two-thirds of California cities shrank in 2025.
